body.statement: At \(C=0\), for every \(T\ge1\), \[\frac{B^2}{T}\le R_T^{(2)}(\beta;B,0)\le\frac{4B^2}{T}.\] The upper bound is attained by independent fair assignments and the periodwise Horvitz--Thompson estimator. The lower bound follows from a prior of independent arm-specific Rademacher endpoints fixed before assignment and is valid for every outcome-adaptive policy. Hence \(R_T^{(2)}(\beta;B,0)=\Theta_B(T^{-1})\).
body.justification: This inherited supporting boundary is the required standard-case reduction and prevents the positive-tail rate from being extrapolated to a degenerate class.
body.gap: The no-memory reduction is already represented in the banked predecessor and finite-order switchback theory; it is retained solely as an audited boundary check.
body.consumer: Practitioners receive a clear diagnostic boundary: if historical sensitivity is absent, ordinary periodwise randomization recovers the parametric MSE rate.
